audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la settimana con un tono positivo, il Nikkei ha guadagnato l'1.8% a 56,924 punti e lo Shanghai ha registrato un aumento dello 0.5% a 4,000 punti. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha chiuso in aumento dello 0.6% a 25,894 punti. Questi dati potrebbero influenzare l'apertura dei mercati europei e americani.

Nella seduta di ieri, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso con una lieve flessione dello 0.1% a 6,800 punti. Il Dollar Index (DXY) ha registrato un calo dello 0.2% a 99 punti. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, ha diminuito dell'1.3% a 19 punti. I tassi di interesse sono stati poco mossi, con il US 10Y Yield che è salito dello 0.6% al 4.3%. L'oro ha perso lo 0.6% a $4,800 l'oncia.

La situazione geopolitica rimane tesa con le notizie di possibili tensioni tra Iran e altri paesi. Questo ha avuto un impatto sui prezzi dell'energia, con il Brent che ha perso lo 0.8% a $95.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, l'attenzione si concentra sui dati che saranno rilasciati prossimamente. Il PIL QoQ USA sarà pubblicato il 29 aprile. In Europa, il tasso BCE (Depositi) è attualmente al 2%. La Global M2 Liquidity continua ad espandersi, con un aumento del 4.9% su base annua.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 

Iniziamo con un deep dive su Bitcoin. La recente performance di Bitcoin ha visto un aumento del 1.5%, portando il prezzo a 72.810 dollari. I flussi degli ETF continuano ad essere positivi, con un inflow giornaliero di 358 milioni di dollari. Questo dato suggerisce una continua fiducia degli investitori istituzionali nel mercato di Bitcoin.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum ha registrato un aumento del 2.2%, raggiungendo il prezzo di 2.235 dollari. Solana e Binance Coin hanno anch'esse mostrato performance positive, con aumenti dell'1.3% e dello 0.9%, portando i prezzi a 84 dollari e 606 dollari rispettivamente.

Per quanto riguarda il sentiment del mercato, l'indice Fear & Greed è attualmente a 15, in territorio di Extreme Fear. Questo livello di paura potrebbe indicare una possibile opportunità di acquisto per gli investitori. La correlazione con i dati macroeconomici recenti, come l'inflazione negli USA, potrebbe influenzare ulteriormente il mercato crypto.

Infine, alcune notizie rilevanti dal mondo crypto includono la discussione sulla possibilità di Bitcoin di garantire un passaggio sicuro attraverso lo stretto di Hormuz e le preoccupazioni riguardo alla possibile introduzione di un pedaggio crypto per le navi petrolifere iraniane. La Casa Bianca ha inoltre avvertito il personale riguardo alle preoccupazioni di insider trading legate alle scommesse iraniane.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is risk-off, with investors cautious amid rising tensions in the Middle East.

Traditional markets are closed for the weekend, but at the last close, equities showed mixed performance. The S&P 500 edged down by 0.1% to 6800, while the STOXX 600 gained 0.3%. Bonds were slightly down, with the TLT Bond USA 20Y at 86, down 0.2%. Currencies saw minor movements, with EUR/USD up 0.3% to 1.2. Commodities were mostly down, with Brent crude oil falling 0.8% to $95 and Gold decreasing 0.6% to $4800/oz.

Geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East, continue to influence market sentiment. Key events include rising oil prices due to the Iran war, which could impact global growth. The ADB warned that developing Asia's growth will slow due to soaring oil prices. On the macro front, global M2 liquidity continues to expand, up 4.9% YoY.

While traditional markets observe their holiday break, the spotlight remains on digital assets, which are open 24/7. Currently, Bitcoin is at $72,815, down 0.2%. Ethereum (ETH) is at $2,235, up 2.2%, and Solana (SOL) is at $84, up 1.3%. The Fear & Greed Index stands at 15, indicating extreme fear. It's essential to monitor these movements as they reflect the current risk sentiment in the digital asset space.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 
    Starting with Bitcoin, it's been a positive day with a 1.5% increase, bringing its current price to $72,810. The recent BTC ETF daily net inflow of $358M suggests growing institutional interest. Despite this, Bitcoin's price action remains cautious, likely influenced by the upcoming economic data releases and the overall market sentiment.

    Moving on to altcoins, we see ETH up 2.2% at $2,235, SOL up 1.3% at $84, and BNB up 0.9% at $606. The altcoin market is showing resilience, with many coins outperforming Bitcoin in terms of percentage gains. However, it's essential to note that the market is still largely correlated with Bitcoin's movements.

    In terms of sentiment and fear/greed, the Fear & Greed Index is currently at 15, indicating extreme fear. This could be a sign that investors are overly cautious, potentially leading to a contrarian buy signal. However, it's crucial to consider the broader market context, including the recent US CPI data and the potential implications for monetary policy. With the PCE Core YoY at 3% and the Core CPI YoY at 2.7%, the economic landscape remains complex, and investors are advised to stay informed and cautious in their approach to the crypto market.

Thanks for tuning in. We'll be back tomorrow with more market insights. Keep an eye on the key events and data releases that could impact your trades. Until then, stay informed and stay ahead. A final word from Prais Alért - have a great day and we'll catch you tomorrow. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Iran war has been an economic gift for Putin
articles.snippet: The Iran war has been an economic gift for Putin Expert comment thilton.drupal 10 April 2026 Higher energy prices and the US decision to ease sanctions on Russian oil have given Moscow a windfall that could help to sustain its war in Ukraine. The US-Israeli war on Iran has been a welcome gift for Russia’s President Vladimir Putin. The war caused an energy crisis as oil and gas prices soared following Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Combined with the US temporarily easing sanctions on Russian oil, surging oil prices have boosted Russia’s budget and export revenues at a time when Western sanctions were hitting Russia’s economy. This windfall will likely increase Russia’s ability to sustain the war against Ukraine. President Putin has also gained increased leverage through h

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. articles.title: Update from the Battlefield: Drones, Distance, and Diminishing Returns for Russia
articles.snippet: Michael Kofman joins Ryan to unpack the current state of the Russo-Ukrainian War after his recent trip to the front. They examine how drone warfare has transformed the battlefield into a dispersed contest over a vast kill zone, why Russian infiltration tactics have failed to produce meaningful gains, and how Ukraine is working to close gaps in its strike capabilities. They also explore the growing pressure from Russian long-range strikes and how the war in Iran is beginning to shape the conflict.Image: ArmyInform via Wikimedia Commons The post Update from the Battlefield: Drones, Distance, and Diminishing Returns for Russia appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Iran’s Other Front: The War Over the Internet
articles.snippet: For a long time, the Iranian government has treated free internet access as a privilege that is extended by the state to those willing to carry its message and withheld from everyone else. Around four hours after Israeli and American strikes began, internet traffic collapsed by 98 percent — a near-total blackout. Iran’s communications infrastructure was deliberately dismantled by the government and internet traffic was completely halted. The strikes were made by the Iranian government’s adversaries aimed at military installations, capabilities, and senior political and military leadership. The internet blackout was imposed by the government, aimed at the Iranian people. The post Iran’s Other Front: The War Over the Internet appeared first on War on the Rocks .
